title: Safety Sentinel: Pin and Fast Rollback Notes (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the "Safety Sentinel" flow: how we pin a model/variant for a short fast rollback window and what signals we watch to auto-failover. Not an official playbook — notes to use for next few canaries.

Context & rationale:
- Want a fast, low-friction escape hatch when a canary causes subtle quality regressions that analytics catch before SLO alerts.
- Pin means route traffic to stable variant while migration/investigation runs.
- Fast rollback should be <5 mins from trigger to routing change (automation preferred).

Preflight checklist (manual quick run):
- [ ] Verify canary build id + model hash in release notes + PR -> GH:1284
- [ ] Confirm canary cohort list (client IDs) in rollout config
- [ ] Sanity smoke test (10 requests): latency, basic correctness, streaming behavior
- [ ] Canary metrics dashboard open (tokens/s, median latency, 99pct, error rate, quality score)
- [ ] Notify oncall + slack short message with anchor link to dashboard

Key thresholds (working heuristics — tune per product):
- Latency: median > baseline + 40ms OR p99 > baseline * 1.5 -> warn
- Errors: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m OR client error spike > 1% -> warn
- Quality regression: eval metric delta > 3% absolute on production prompt set -> critical
- User complaints (support tags): 3 unique complaint threads in 10m -> investigate

Fast rollback flow (automated + manual steps):
1) Signal detection -> webhook to rollout service (alerts via PagerDuty + slack).
2) Pre-approval window (30s): check for spurious spikes (if ephemeral, don't rollback).
3) If persistent for 3 consecutive windows (1m windows) -> trigger pin+rolloff:
    - Call rollout API: POST /v1/rollouts/pin {route, from:canary, to:stable, reason}
    - Annotate release tag as rolled-back and create ticket REL-XXXX if not present
4) Confirm traffic split now 100% stable variant for that cohort; run targeted smoke tests
5) Kick off investigate/rollforward plan, retain canary logs and KV cache snapshot for debugging

Sample CLI (rough):
# check current split
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rollouts/route/my-service | jq .
# pin to stable
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"my-service","from":"canary-2026-03-08","to":"stable-2026-02-14","force":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rollouts/pin

Observability artifacts to snapshot (minutes 0,5,30):
- Trace sample set (top 10 traces by latency)
- Model output diffs for golden prompts (save to S3 under rel-4592/canary-diffs)
- KV cache hit/miss ratio and token distribution
- System metrics: GPU util, mem pressure, OOM events

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- Can we reduce false positives from short-lived p99 spikes caused by noisy region? Proposal: require region-coherent signal (>=2 zones) or global increase.
- How to surface model-quality regressions faster (heartbeat eval set more representative of real traffic).
- Add a small pre-warm step to canary (2% warm traffic for 5m) to avoid cold-kv spikes.
- Verify the rollout API supports immediate revert without audit friction (ask platform eng).

Notes to self after last run (2026-01-21):
- Triggered pin due to quality metric; automation worked but rollback left stale client affinity cookie leading to 2% of clients still hitting old canary -> need affinity invalidation step.
- Add affinity-expire call in post-pin checklist.

Quick micro playbook (one-liner for oncall):
- If quality or error thresholds cross: run `pin-to-stable --route my-service --reason "auto-sentinel"` then `invalidate-client-affinity --route my-service` and post to #releases with timestamp + rr.

References/links (bookmarks):
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284 (canary rollout changes)
- JIRA: REL-4592 (agent observed quality regressions investigation)
- Confluence: 'Release Playbook v2' (section: fast rollback)

End of scratchpad. Keep short, iterate next run.

(Notes are informal — copy to official playbook if we confirm heuristics.)
